newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LSWR eases on Indonesia's 3.5 mln bbls, HSFO hold.
newsitem.headline: LSWR eases on Indonesia's 3.5 mln bbls, HSFO hold.

text.p: Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) dominated fuel oil market discussion with a total of 3.5 million barrels expected in Indonesia's January allocation, traders said on Thursday.
They said British Petroleum (BP) has been allocated 1.1 million barrels but other details, including the loading schedule were not yet available.
Traders said LSWR prices, currently assessed at $23-$23.2 per barrel are likely to ease further in January as they expect Pertamina to allocate a further 500,000 barrels in January at a later date.
They said the total of 4 million barrels would be sufficient to meet demand as requirements from Japan and the west is expected to less in January.
High sulphur fuel oil prices were supported by gains seen on Tuesday's crude prices.
February Brent crude closed up 20 cents to $23.40 a barrel on Tuesday.
The market is also very quiet as some traders were still away for holidays.
January fuel oil swap was talked firmer in quiet trading and was quoted at $$120.50/$121.50 per tonne, up from Tuesday's $119.50/$121.00.
